about: Act 1's still plates: where every picture came from (04-asset-plan.md, section 1). Rejected takes stay in _takes/images (ignored by git). Prompts: scripts/images/prompts.json. Second cut (v2): every generation is listed with a status; takes are in out/act1-v2/takes (ignored by git); prompts in scripts/images/prompts-v2.json; finals in public/img/v2.

No text, no letters, no digits, no symbols, no logos, no brand marks, no people, no hands.

Compared by eye with the well-known candybar, flip and slider handsets of 1998-2005: no navigation key, call keys, aerial, grille, plate or signature shape, so not mistakable for any of them.

images.prompt: Image 1 is a line drawing of a product. Turn it into a photorealistic photograph of that product. Preserve the exact layout, proportions and perspective of the drawing; do not add new elements or text. The phone: an ordinary keypad mobile phone from about 2004, an invented design that copies no real model and carries no brand. A slim bar 106 mm tall, 46 mm wide and 19 mm thick: a softly rounded rectangle with 8 mm corner radii, gently rounded side edges and a smooth top edge with no aerial. Front cover in satin pewter-grey painted plastic with a faint metallic fleck; a thin seam runs around the sides where it meets the darker charcoal back cover. On the front, from top to bottom: a short horizontal earpiece slot; a clear acrylic lens with a thin black printed border around a small monochrome display, 34 mm wide and 26 mm tall, switched off, dark olive-grey glass showing no image; a row with a small pill-shaped key at each side and, between them, a round four-way navigation key with a separate round centre button; a second pill-shaped key at each side below the first; then twelve identical keys in three columns and four rows, each a wide rounded rectangle about 12.5 by 6.5 mm, in dark charcoal translucent rubber with a satin coating, evenly spaced in a straight grid; a tiny microphone hole near the bottom edge. Used for years: hairline scratches and fine swirl marks on the acrylic lens, a few deeper scratches, paint worn through to darker plastic on the corners, the most-used keys polished smooth and slightly glossy in the middle, a little grime in the seams. Scene: the phone lies face up on a dark matte surface, photographed from directly above with the lens axis exactly perpendicular to its face, from far away with a long lens so its edges stay parallel; centred, long side vertical, filling 90% of the frame height. Soft moonlight from the upper left grazes the keys and the lens; its reflection falls outside the display window. A real photograph, not a render or an illustration. Night in a dark room; the only light is cool, soft moonlight from a window at the upper left, with deep blue-violet shadows and natural falloff. Full-frame camera, 100 mm macro lens, ISO 3200, fine natural grain, subtle lens vignette. Muted, slightly desaturated colour. No studio lighting, no rim lights, no lens flare. Every key and the whole body are completely unprinted: no digits, no letters, no symbols, no icons, no logo, no brand name, no sticker, no text anywhere in the picture. No hands, no people. No curved or tilted key rows, no oval or teardrop keys, no joystick, no aerial, no patterned or coloured cover.
images.notes: Master. Real keypad-phone anatomy from the line drawing; keys and body blank at 100%; dark scratched screen; worn corners. More contrast and wear than take 04.
